thread:
perf-ci-bot: CI microbench threshold FAILED on PR #15001 (merge candidate). Test: batch_sampler_latency_micro. Noise-filtered diff +18% vs golden. Artifacts: <https://ci.redwood.example/15001/artifacts>

Maria: seeing the alert — can anyone repro locally?

Sam: repro on my dev-3 (A100). quick bench run below, short summary attached.

Sam: ```
$ bench run batch_sampler --iter 1000
median latency: 8.4ms -> baseline 7.1ms (+18%)
p50/p95/p99: 7.9/12.3/20.1
alloc: 12MB -> 45MB
CPU: kernel_sampler hot
```

Jordan: interesting — I noticed elevated python GC collections in the distributed traces for the same PR. Could be GC churn from the new sampler allocations.

Maria: I pulled the CI flametrace. KV cache miss rate also ticked up ~+7% around the same window. Not sure if related.

Sam: profiler top lines:```
# hot functions (sampled)
kernel_sampler: 42%
cpu_copy_async: 12%
pyobject_alloc: 9%   <-- GC churn
```

Jordan: PR included two commits: 9a7c3b (adaptive sampler heuristics) and 9b8d1e (python wrapper refactor that changes allocation site). They landed together in the feature branch.

Maria: which one do we suspect? my hunch is the wrapper refactor — it introduced a small object that seems to be getting created per-batch.

Jordan: agree. wrapper refactor is smaller surface area. suggest revert 9b8d1e first and run CI microbench again.

Sam: running a quick local with the wrapper reverted (manual patch) — will post numbers in ~20m.

perf-ci-bot: Started rerun job job/4744321001 (abbrev: rerun-15001) on canary infra.

Maria: if local confirms, we should mark this as rollout-blocker and open a revert PR asap. Also add `perf/regression` label.

Sam: update — local rerun with wrapper revert:```
median latency: 7.2ms (baseline 7.1ms)
alloc: 13MB
p95: 11.9ms
KV cache miss: back to baseline
```

Sam: looks like the wrapper refactor was the culprit (large alloc churn). I'll open a revert PR for 9b8d1e now.

Jordan: once revert PR merges, let's canary rollout to 10% and run the full golden microbench suite (seqlen distributions included) — KV warmup can hide regressions.

Maria: agreed. also please add a short note in the PR description: observed GC churn + alloc spike + KV miss bump. link to profiler flamegraph.

Alex: got the ping. I'll hold the release window until the revert PR is validated on CI. Thanks for the fast triage. :thumbsup:

Sam: opened revert PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/15002 — assigning Jordan for quick review.

Jordan: reviewing now. if green, will approve and request canary deploy.

perf-ci-bot: rerun job/4744321001 finished: microbench suite green (within thresholds).

Maria: closing the thread for now — follow-up: add a unit test that asserts no per-batch pyobject allocations in the hot path (or at least a budget).

Sam: filing issue #3425 for the test.

Maria: nice work all, good triage and quick revert.
